title: entitlements-and-purchase-pathways-playbook-2029
author: Maya Chen
content:
> **Archived 2026-11-12:** this page is superseded by "entitlements-and-purchase-pathways-playbook-2030" and is kept for reference only.

Overview
========

Purpose: This playbook brings together Redwood's procedures for entitlements (access and permissions), change governance, data handling, procurement and expense approvals, vendor lifecycle management, and travel approvals. It applies to every employee and contractor who requests or approves resources, pushes changes to production, or manages a third-party relationship.

Scope: Hosted, dedicated, and private deployment teams; platform and infra teams; procurement; people-ops travel; and any third party that will touch Redwood systems or customer data.

Quick links: Access Portal (Okta + Access Request), VendorHub (procurement back-end), ExpenseFlow (employee expenses), Legal intake form, Security questionnaire (security.redwood.local).

Roles and responsibilities
--------------------------

- Requestor: starts the access, change, purchase, vendor, or travel request and owns its completeness and business justification.
- Manager/Approver: the direct manager, who confirms business need and available budget.
- Approving Officer (Finance/Procurement): checks procurement thresholds, tax, and vendor classification.
- Security Reviewer: assesses data access risk and required controls (SOC2, encryption, contract clauses).
- Legal Reviewer: reviews vendor contracts above threshold or with custom IP/data terms.
- Proc Ops (Vendor Onboarding): completes supplier setup and collects W-9/COI where applicable.

Principles
----------

- Least privilege: grant only the entitlements needed and set expirations wherever practical.
- Segregation of duties: for medium/high risk requests, the same person may not both approve and provision.
- Evidence-first approvals: every approval is attached to its request in VendorHub or Access Portal.
- Risk proportionality: tighter controls for vendors with data access, privileged infra access, or spend above financial thresholds.

Access & permissions (entitlement lifecycle)
-------------------------------------------

1) Request process

- Submit requests through the Access Portal (Redwood Console > Tools > Access Request).
- Include justification, target systems (service and environment), the exact RBAC role, duration, and manager approval.
- Roles held longer than 90 days need a quarterly business justification and a named reviewer in Access Portal.

2) Approval matrix (summary)

- Non-prod access: manager approval.
- Prod read-only: manager approval plus security notification.
- Prod privileged/infra (SSH, K8s-admin, DB write): manager, security, and infra-owner approval.
- Emergency elevated access: follow the break-glass procedure (Runbook ID: RG-2026-breakglass).

3) Provisioning and deprovisioning

- Okta + Terraform runbooks (Infra-IAC) provision access automatically once approved. Provisioning SLA is 3 business days for standard requests and 8 hours for emergency sprints.
- Expirations are enforced: 30 days by default for contractor requests and 90 days for internal hires unless renewed.

4) Periodic review

- Quarterly access attestation: team owners confirm active entitlements and remove stale accounts. Non-response triggers automated revocation notices.

Change management
-----------------

Scope: Any change to production services, infra provisioning, IAM policies, or customer-facing configuration.

Change categories and approval paths:

- Standard change: pre-approved, repeatable work (e.g., routine OS patching through the controlled pipeline). Needs a change ticket and a notice to SRE runbook subscribers.
- Normal change: higher-impact work (planned releases affecting SLAs) needs Change Review Board (CRB) approval. CRB meets twice weekly.
- Emergency change: urgent fixes follow the emergency roll-forward checklist and are documented in the change ticket afterwards.

Change windows and freezes:

- Quarterly freeze: the last two business days of each quarter are frozen for major releases unless the CTO and SRE lead approve an exception.
- High-risk releases: canary rollout with 30% traffic validation for 24 hours before full rollout.

Change request minimum content (ticket):

1. Change owner and contact
2. Rollout and rollback plan, including automation steps
3. Expected impact and post-deploy validation
4. Backout criteria and timeline
5. Stakeholders to notify

Audit

- Every normal change must have a ticket and remain auditable for 12 months.
- Emergency changes should be documented promptly after the fix.

Data management and classification
--------------------------------

Classification levels:

- Public: meant for public consumption.
- Internal: operational information not for external distribution.
- Confidential: employee, business, or customer information requiring access controls.
- Restricted: regulated or highly sensitive data (PII, payment, health) requiring encryption at rest and in transit, strict access control, and audit logging.

Handling rules (summary):

- Confidential & Restricted: keep only in approved systems (Redwood Console vaults, encrypted S3 with KMS). No transfer to vendors without security and legal sign-off.
- Retention: logs are kept 90 days by default; customer-facing telemetry follows contractual obligations.
- Deletion: submit a Data Erasure Request and confirm via the automated deletion job.

Procurement and expenses
------------------------

Purchase approval thresholds (effective):

| Amount (USD) | Approvals required | Notes |
|--------------|-------------------|-------|
| < 1,000 | Manager | Auto-approval in VendorHub if budget tag present |
| 1,000 – 25,000 | Manager + Finance | Finance checks budget and tax classification |
| > 25,000 | Manager + Finance + Procurement + Legal | Requires exec sponsor and procurement intake form |

Procurement steps:

1. Open a VendorHub request with business justification, vendor name, SOW/quote, and budget tag.
2. Attach vendor compliance documents (SOC2, ISO, insurance certificate) if available.
3. Finance confirms budget and tax treatment within 3 business days.
4. Procurement routes requests >25k or with non-standard T&Cs to Legal.
5. After approval, Procurement issues the purchase order and coordinates supplier setup.

Expense reimbursement:

- Submit in ExpenseFlow with receipts within 30 days of the expense. Per diem caps: domestic $125/day, international $250/day unless pre-approved. Corporate cards are preferred for travel; personal card reimbursements need manager approval.

Vendor management lifecycle
--------------------------

Onboarding checklist (timeline expectations):

- Intake: vendor submitted via VendorHub, acknowledged within 1 business day.
- Risk assessment: Security reviews the questionnaire; plan on 5-7 business days for standard vendors and 15-20 days for vendors handling Restricted data.
- Contracting: Legal drafts/negotiates; low-risk vendors use standard NDA/SOW templates. Expect 5-15 business days.
- Procurement & finance: vendor setup (W-9/COI), tax classification, payment terms.

Minimum vendor requirements by risk tier:

- Low risk (no data access): PO, standard SOE, vendor contact, invoice cadence.
- Medium risk (limited data access): PO, signed DPA, security questionnaire, SOC2 Type II preferred.
- High risk (customer data or privileged infra access): PO, DPA, SOC2 Type II or penetration test report, system access plan, breach notification clause, indemnity terms.

Offboarding and termination:

- Revoke credentials, recover assets, enforce data return/deletion, reconcile the final invoice, and obtain post-termination confirmation from the vendor. Procurement keeps termination evidence for 7 years.

Travel policy (high level)
-------------------------

Booking: Use the Travel Portal (linked from Redwood Console). Lowest reasonable economy fare applies. Business class needs exec-level pre-approval for trips over 8 hours.

Approvals: Managers approve travel in the Travel Portal. International trips to high-risk countries on the People Ops list require security and people-ops notification.

Per diems and expenses: See ExpenseFlow caps above. Receipts are required for any item >$25.

Safety and incident reporting:

- If an incident occurs while traveling, contact the People Ops emergency line and Security (security@redwood.com) within 24 hours.

Templates and forms (where to find)
----------------------------------

- Procurement intake form: VendorHub > New Request > Procurement Intake (template 'Procurement-Intake-v1').
- Data Erasure Request: Redwood Console > Data Requests.
- Change request template: CRB ticket template in Jira (project: RED-CHANGES).
- Access request template: Access Portal (choose role and environment).

Example procurement JSON payload (for VendorHub API)

{
  "requestor": "alice@example.com",
  "vendor": "Acme Analytics",
  "amount_usd": "7500",
  "justification": "Production observability for dedicated clusters",
  "budget_tag": "infra-monitoring",
  "required_by": "2026-10-15"
}

Appendix: enforcement and exceptions
-----------------------------------

- Exceptions: Managers can request a documented exception for short-lived needs, backed by a written business case and compliance review.
- Enforcement: Repeated violations (e.g., unmanaged vendor engagements or expired privileged access) are escalated to the employee's manager and may lead to procurement suspension or disciplinary review.

Contacts and ownership
----------------------

- Policy owner: Finance-Legal (procurement@redwood.com).
- Vendor risk security contact: security@redwood.com.
- People Ops travel & benefits: people-ops@redwood.com.
